texts.preamble: M/S.Dry Nut Enterprises vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 30 June, 2022 Author: Anita Sumanth
texts.facts: Respondents in both Common Prayer:Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution India, to issue a Writ of Mandamus, directing the respondents herein to the goods viz., 675 Bags viz., 54,000 Mts., and 1013 bags viz., 81.000 M of Betel Nut Products (known as (Supari Unflavoured) Cutting of Indonesi Origin imported from The Republic of Indonesia vide Bill of Entry Nos.7667388, 7667284, dated 27.02.2022, classifiable under CTH 21069030 and totally valued at USD 81,000.00 (CIF) for 54,000 Mts and USD 121,500.00 (CIF) for 81.000 Mts and further direct the respondents to is waiver certificate for detention and demurrage charges under Regulations Handling of Cargo in Customs Areas Regulations 2009. In both W.Ps. For Petitioner : Mr.A.K.Jayaraj For Respondents: Mrs.R.Hemalatha Senior Standing Counsel R1 to R4 Mr.V.Sundareswaran Senior Panel Counsel R5 COMMON ORDER Mrs.R.Hemalatha, learned Senior Standing Counsel accepts notice for R1 to R4 and Mr.V.Sundareswaran, learned Senior Panel counsel accepts notice for R5. 2. The petitioner seeks a mandamus directing the respondents to release the goods viz., 675 Bags viz., 54,000 Mts., (W.P.No.16260 of 2022) and 1013 bags viz., 81.000 Mts., (W.P.No.16267 of 2022) of Betel Nut Products (known as (Supari Unflavoured) imported from Indonesia vide Bill of Entry Nos.7667388 (W.P.No.16260 of 2022) and 7667284 (W.P.No.16267 of 2022), both dated 27.02.2022, classifiable under CTH 21069030 and totally valued at USD 81,000.00 (CIF) for 54,000 Mts and USD 121,500.00 (CIF) for 81.000 Mts and further direct the respondents to issue M/S.Dry Nut Enterprises vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 30 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133033765/ 2 waiver certificate for detention and demurrage charges under Regulations of Handling of Cargo in Customs Areas Regulations 2009. 3.
texts.arguments: However, the provisions of Section 125, that deals with 'option to pay fine in view of confiscation' provides for two situations. In the case of confiscation of prohibited goods, the option to pay fine in lieu of confiscation is discretionary, such discretion to be exercised by the authority. 15. It is only in the case of other goods, that are not prohibited, that the Officer shall offer to the owner or the person from whose possession the goods were seized, an option to pay a fine, in lieu of confiscation. Thus, in the case of prohibited goods, the d i s c r e t i o n a s t o w h e t h e r f i n e m a y b e i m p o s e d i n l i e u o f https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis WP.Nos.16260 and 16267 of 2022 and WMP Nos.15604 and 15608 of 2022 confiscation is that of the officer concerned.
